wins: Collected initial host and service discovery data
Maintained positive reward despite overall failure
fails: High mentor call count indicates reliance and decision uncertainty
key_outcomes.summary: Single-episode run achieved partial reconnaissance progress but failed to convert into a successful outcome; needs tighter decision-making and exploitation follow-through.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Stalled after reconnaissance without selecting a concrete exploitation path
Over-reliance on mentor guidance before executing actions

skill_cards.if_condition: When initial host discovery is required on an unknown network segment
skill_cards.then_action: Run a fast ping sweep to identify live hosts

skill_cards.if_condition: When live hosts are identified and service inventory is needed
skill_cards.then_action: Perform targeted TCP service enumeration on common ports

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP/HTTPS is detected on a target host
skill_cards.then_action: Run web content discovery to map endpoints

memory_ops.reason: Consistent early-stage host discovery sets up subsequent enumeration.
Service enumeration is a necessary bridge between discovery and exploitation.

next_experiments.title: Exploit path selection drill
next_experiments.description: After service enumeration, force a single exploit hypothesis (e.g., weak SSH, web vuln) and execute a full attempt before branching.

next_experiments.title: Mentor call reduction challenge
next_experiments.description: Limit mentor calls to 3 and document decision rationale for each action to build autonomy.

next_experiments.title: Web-focused exploitation follow-through
next_experiments.description: If HTTP is found, complete a full cycle: content discovery → vuln scan (e.g., nikto) → exploit attempt.
